methodological_rigor.justification: The study has a clear proof-of-concept structure and includes a held-out test set, but the biological design is severely constrained by having only one pediatric GBM line, SF188, versus five adult lines. The classifier may therefore be learning cell-line-specific differences rather than a general pediatric-versus-adult signature, and no independent biological validation is shown.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an in vitro preclinical study, so Oxford level 5 is the correct classification under the rubric. The translational relevance is only speculative at this stage because the work is a label-free diagnostic proof of concept in cell lines, not a patient-facing assay or validated clinical workflow.

reporting_quality.justification: No established reporting checklist clearly applies beyond the general expectations for a preclinical methods paper, so none is the best fit here. The manuscript gives substantial acquisition and modeling detail, but it does not state any public data or code availability, and the reporting is weakened by the very limited biological replication across age groups.

novelty_literature.justification: The novel element is the use of confocal Raman spectroscopy plus a neural network to distinguish pediatric from adult glioblastoma stem-cell models using intrinsic biochemical fingerprints. That is a genuine methodological and empirical extension of prior Raman-oncology work, although the paper still builds on an existing literature of Raman classification and glioma deep learning.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is understandable overall, but it is very verbose, repetitive, and occasionally awkward in phrasing, and several sections read like extended explanation rather than concise scientific reporting. The abstract and figures communicate the basic point, yet the overall presentation is not polished enough for a stronger score.

key_strengths: Novel Raman-plus-deep-learning approach for pediatric versus adult GBM discrimination
Held-out test evaluation with preprocessing confined to the training data
Clear spectral feature interpretation tied to lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids
key_concerns: Only one pediatric biological model, so generalizability is weak
No patient-level validation or clinical deployment data
Writing is verbose and the translational claim is ahead of the evidence
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a promising proof-of-concept with real technical novelty, but the biological design is too narrow to support strong claims about pediatric GBM as a class. It is most plausible in a lower-tier, methods-oriented venue after substantial revision.
